short: Serbian forces defeated an Austro-Hungarian invasion, marking the first Allied victory of the war.
full:
On 15 August 1914, Austro-Hungarian forces advancing into Serbia encountered the Serbian army on the slopes of Cer Mountain. Despite being significantly outnumbered and underequipped, the experienced Serbians launched a fierce counter-attack. Over ten days of intense, often hand-to-hand combat in difficult terrain, the Serbians broke the Austro-Hungarian lines and forced them into a chaotic retreat across the Drina river.

The Battle of Cer was the first major Allied victory of the First World War. It humiliated the Austro-Hungarian command and temporarily secured Serbia's independence. However, the heavy casualties sustained by both sides foreshadowed the attritional campaigns that would eventually devastate the Balkans.
